content:
- Overestimate prices in the short term after positive sentiment spikes; model tends to overshoot early in the 30-day horizon.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., -1.13 or lower) — model fails to account for downward momentum.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: overreacts to recent price spikes, then forecasts a sharp drop that doesn’t materialize.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (e.g., 0.31, 0.34), model often underestimates the true decline — fails to recognize risk-off or policy-driven corrections.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag in price correction: model takes 2–3 days to adjust downward after sentiment turns negative.
- After a spike (e.g., 75+), model overcorrects downward, then fails to recover — underestimates rebound potential.
- Sentiment history with multiple consecutive positive values (e.g., 1.09, 1.13) leads to overconfident forecasts — model ignores volatility clustering.
- When sentiment turns negative after a spike, model delays correction — often underestimates the depth of the drop.
- Model tends to ignore sentiment shifts in the last 3–5 days of history — overweights earlier sentiment, leading to misaligned forecasts.
